title: Cache skeletonization: spine-prefetch & kernel co-placement for low-fragmentation paged KV
creator: Leah Park
description: Motivation: Pager-based KV caches for paged attention suffer from fragmentation and allocation churn when interleaved prefill and decode waves target discontiguous token spans. This ticket proposes a lightweight 'skeletonization' layer (spine allocator + transient adjacency hints) that reduces fragmentation, guides prefetch windows, and enables kernel co-placement decisions to reduce decode latency and prefill overhead across multi-tenant workloads. The goal is to lower end-to-end 95th percentile decode latency by reducing prefills and cross-shard kernel handoffs while keeping steady-state memory overhead small.
technical_design: Core idea: maintain a thin spine index per KV shard that records recent adjacency relationships between pages (hot-span chains) and a compact activity histogram. On allocation, the spine allocator prefers filling slots adjacent to a chain root to form contiguous micro-runs; when contiguous allocation is impossible, allocation falls back to best-fit-scored fragments. The spine exposes a small API to the prefill planner: (1) suggest_prefetch_windows(token_span) -> ordered page list, (2) recommend_kernel_grouping(page_list) -> kernel affinity tags. Prefetch planner uses the suggested windows to schedule prefill tasks with staggered deadlines and to avoid simultaneous reclamation-sensitive prefetch bursts. Kernel co-placement uses affinity tags to bias kernel selection so that pages likely to be used together are compiled/allocated onto the same kernel lane or GPU slice when possible.
tradeoffs_and_constraints:
- Tradeoff: slightly increased allocation latency (microseconds) due to spine bookkeeping vs. reduced decode jitter. We limit spine updates to the allocation hot path and perform decay/compaction asynchronously.
- Constraint: limited metadata budget per shard (~64 bytes/page). Spine metadata must be compact and relocatable across rebalances.
- Compatibility: works with existing paged-attn prefill API; requires small proto change to prefill planner to accept affinity tags.
- Multi-tenant fairness: spine must be tenant-scoped to avoid noisy-neighbor hijacking; use per-tenant soft quotas and tenant-weighted scoring.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype spine data structure in simulator and run mixed-workload traces (see testing_plan). 2) Add spine allocator MVP to runtime allocator with feature flag. 3) Integrate spine->prefill hints with prefill planner API (feature gated). 4) Expose kernel affinity suggestions to kernel scheduler and extend kernel selector heuristics to prefer co-placement where capacity permits. 5) Canary on internal staging cluster with 5% traffic, monitor latency, prefill counts, memory overhead. 6) Roll to 25% then 100% with rollback if 95th latency regresses >5% or prefill traffic increases >10% over baseline.
testing_plan:
- Simulator: run 72-hour mixed tenant traces with span distributions (short chat, long context, bursty autocomplete) to measure fragmentation, contiguous-run length, prefill count, and simulated kernel handoffs.
- Unit tests: spine metadata lifetime, decay behavior, and allocator fallback correctness.
- Integration: end-to-end staging runs with canary workloads (internal bots) to measure decode p95, token throughput, and memory peak.
- Load test: spike scenarios (10x concurrent prefill) to validate backpressure and prefill staggering keep SLOs intact.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator: 30-50% reduction in page-fragmentation index across representative traces compared to baseline
Staging: no increase in overall memory peak beyond 5% of baseline
Staging: decode P95 reduced by at least 3% and decode P99 not regressed
Operational: prefill count per decode reduced by >= 10% for long-context workloads
Feature gates: rollouts and rollbacks executable without service interruption
